fields.RequiredArtifact: One owner-accepted V1 branch. **Branch A:** a public AI Party type and an authorization contract permitting only the Agents Service Principal to create `hexa`'s deterministic provisioned Party under that type. **Branch B:** Parties Maintainer and Product formally accept the existing Organization-typed provisioned Party as the V1 launch contract, verified everywhere by its immutable deterministic id and never by type. Both branches require create-only AD-2 provisioning, idempotent exact retries, typed conflict for divergent identity/type requests, mandatory tenant scope, no tenant-role creation or replacement, and no Party PII in public results. The record must name the selected branch; absence of that decision is `Uncommitted`. Independently of the selected identity branch, Parties exposes a tenant-scoped authoritative resolution by `PartyId` returning stable Party classification (`Human`, `Organization`, or `AI`), active/liveness state, evidence position and observed instant, plus typed missing, ambiguous, stale, denied, and unavailable outcomes. For every human Party, the same seam also returns one stable non-PII `AuthenticatedHumanActorId`, `HumanActorBindingVersion`, validity interval, and queryable binding history sufficient to reproduce the identity in force at an action; it returns typed missing, ambiguous, stale, and overlapping-history outcomes. AD-8 uses both classification and binding at predefined-approver configuration and every runtime approver resolution; non-human Parties can never be Approvers, and a human command carrying a Party must bind to the same authenticated actor id.
fields.CompatibilityContractAndVerificationComm: Contract: for the selected branch, create and resolve exactly one deterministic tenant-scoped provisioned Party for `hexa` under the Agents Service Principal; verify immutable identity by id on every path and additionally verify AI type only for Branch A; reject tenant-role creation, cross-tenant access, divergent replay, and replacement; return typed safe outcomes without Party PII; resolve approver candidates to fresh authoritative human-type and active/liveness evidence; resolve each human Party to its stable `AuthenticatedHumanActorId` and binding version; reproduce the binding in force for a historical instant; and reject missing, stale, ambiguous, overlapping, or actor-mismatched bindings with typed fail-closed outcomes. Command: `TBD`.
fields.ConsumingStories: `RQ-1`; Stories 5.2, 5.4, 5.5, 6.1, 6.6, 7.1–7.5, 8.1–8.4, and 8.8 directly or conditionally consume identity or human Party/liveness/binding evidence. Story 6.1 directly verifies the caller and provisioned Agent Party and executes FR-8 membership step 10; Story 5.5's consumption remains conditional on the Product-selected recorder scope; Story 8.4 consumes the Release-Operator review branch. Branch-B-compatible identity-by-id portions may be developed where applicable, but no consumer may cite that work or any human actor-binding seam as launch evidence while this record is `Uncommitted`

fields.Owner: Project owner (user declaration 2026-10-07), acting as Conversations Maintainer
fields.RequiredArtifact: Six core V1 seams. (1) Membership: public `IConversationClient.AddParticipantAsync` and `POST /api/v1/conversations/{conversationId}/participants`, limited for Agents to stable AI Party identity, `ParticipantType.AiAgent`, and `ParticipantRole.Member`; exact retries are idempotent no-ops, conflicting type/role is a typed conflict, and cross-tenant or general participant management is denied; plus a participant-state read for the AI participant and a participant removal limited to the AI participant for the PRD FR-2 removal block. Before accepting membership, Conversations verifies the immutable provisioned Party by id and additionally verifies AI type only when `EXT-PARTIES-1` commits Branch A; Branch B accepts its approved Organization type by id; the record owner supplies the final member and typed failure names (A-21). (2) Posting: append a Conversation Message as the `AiAgent` participant with an Agents-supplied deterministic `MessageId` and idempotency key, persisted verbatim or rejected (a differing returned id is a typed incompatibility that blocks posting), and message metadata carrying the Agent Call trace reference and provenance flags (AI-generated; human-edited and by which Party), so restart or replay cannot duplicate a post; plus an existence read by `MessageId` returning the message, typed absence, typed `ConversationDeleted`, typed `PrincipalRemovedFromConversation`, or unavailable, so Agents can check before retry or abandonment after a lost acknowledgement and record `LateConfirmed` rather than contradict an already-posted message. (3) Facilitator resolution: `ParticipantRole.Facilitator` on the participant read model. (4) The Eligible Conversation denominator is supplied either as an active-Conversation count per tenant/window or as a Conversations-side tenant event feed from which Agents computes the same count, never from Agent Calls (A-4). (5) Tenant-scoped reads under the Agents Service Principal of complete Conversation content, the Participant roster with roles, and Conversation existence/accessibility; they return typed `ConversationDeleted` and `PrincipalRemovedFromConversation` distinctly from transient denial or error, and content contains the messages a Participant would currently see, including current edit/delete state (A-15). (6) A Conversations-owned durable outbox or ordered tenant/source feed entry created atomically with the approved Conversation-deletion decision. It carries one immutable `ConversationDeletionSignalId` bound one-to-one to that logical approval, `TenantId`, `ConversationId`, stable source stream/revision, approval reference, source-contract version, and an independent delivery-attempt id. Reconnect/backfill is ordered from a durable checkpoint; the source retains and retries the same logical entry through Agents outage, typed refusal, target-version rollover, and lost acknowledgement until authenticated `DeletionSignalAccepted(SignalId, SourceRevision, ProtectedDeletionRevision)` advances the checkpoint. Retransmission never mints a new signal id/source revision; changed fields at the same id are a quarantined compatibility conflict that is not skipped or acknowledged, blocks seam readiness, and exposes only safe poison metadata. Source-revision and Agents acknowledgement lookup resolve both sides of lost delivery. The authenticated source identity and exact target are verified before Agents dispatch; the signal triggers PRD FR-30 deletion of derived Agent content and never grants a human Agents role, local cancellation authority, or scope beyond that source Conversation. Final member and typed failure names are owned by this record (PRD §8.1 assumptions A-1 through A-4, A-15, A-16, A-21).
fields.CompatibilityContractAndVerificationComm: Contract: typed idempotent membership with participant-state read, AI-participant removal, and Hexalith.Parties identity-by-id verification plus AI-type verification only under committed Branch A; idempotent posting with trace/provenance metadata and a typed `MessageId` existence read covering message, absence, deletion, principal removal, and unavailable; Facilitator role exposure; active-Conversation count or equivalent Conversations-side tenant event feed; tenant-scoped current content/roster/existence/accessibility reads that distinguish deletion/removal from transient denial/error; and atomic durable approved-deletion outbox/feed delivery with stable logical signal/source revision, ordered checkpoint/backfill, retry until authenticated Agents acknowledgement, target-version rollover, conflict quarantine/no-skip, acknowledgement/source lookup, local-cancellation denial, and focused cross-tenant denial. Command: `TBD`.

fields.Owner: Project owner (user declaration 2026-10-07), acting as Platform Maintainer
fields.RequiredArtifact: Versioned secret custody for Provider credentials, per-tenant KEKs and DigestKeys, tenant migration-epoch/directory-effect capability signing keys with exact revocation state, the reserved-system security-observation digest key, per-export envelope keys, manifest-signing keys/public trust anchors, trusted-envelope HMAC keys, and decision-authority verification anchors/trust profile. Decision-approval signing keys remain outside Agents and platform-host custody under the independently governed issuer named by that profile; the profile binds issuer, stable actor/authority-role sources for Product, Governance, Security, Architecture, and named maintainers, key-use purpose, freshness/expiry/revocation, and forbids the Release Operator recorder or platform key custodian from requesting or minting approval evidence. The trusted-envelope profile fixes issuer/audience, numeric maximum tag lifetime, clock skew, rotation overlap, command retry/recovery horizon, and `ReplayRecordRetention` no shorter than the greater of tag lifetime plus skew plus overlap and that recovery horizon, consumed by the Agents-owned reserved-`system` `TrustedEnvelopeReplay(Issuer, DeliveryNonce)` aggregate whose record binds the authenticated target tenant; it also fixes active/revoked key state, emergency revocation, retained digest-key versions, decision-manifest verification, wrap/unwrap/pin/unpin/destroy operations with irreversible receipts, safe rotation/invalidation signals, and a principal-bound `DeliverExportKey(DeliveryId, ExportId, CommitAcknowledgementRevision, RequesterActorId, Purpose, Audience, ExclusiveExpiry, LifecycleVersion, StoreTarget, ContractVersion)` operation whose key bytes are delivered directly to that authenticated principal. Delivery is idempotent by the complete identity and exposes authenticated exact outcome lookup as `Delivered(ObservedAt)`, `NotDelivered(Reason)`, or `Unknown/Unavailable`; the custodian rejects cross-tenant, changed-identity, expired, or revoked authority before release. Only opaque references, versions, public anchors, policy bounds, and configured/not-configured state cross Agents boundaries.
fields.CompatibilityContractAndVerificationComm: Contract: platform-hosted versioned resolution and custody; AES-256-GCM export-key wrapping; RFC 7515/7518 ES256 manifest signing and offline public-anchor verification; HMAC-SHA-256 trusted-envelope issuance/constant-time verification over AD-30 canonical bytes; target-tenant migration epoch/directory-effect capability issuance and legacy-epoch revocation accepted by the EventStore append guard; system-keyed HMAC of untrusted security-observation fields; independently issued signed decision-governance/authority manifests binding exact contract/version, effective predecessor or root policy, nonempty required approvers, affected evaluations, stable actor/role evidence, freshness, and revocation, with tests proving neither recorder nor custodian can sign/request approval; immutable `LogicalCommandId`, issuer-wide unique per-delivery `DeliveryNonce`, byte-identical replay routed only to domain idempotency, changed-field or cross-tenant nonce reuse rejected in the reserved-system replay namespace, bounded expiry/skew/overlap with retained replay records across the complete bound, emergency-revocation redispatch under a new key and nonce, rotation-triggered safety-verdict invalidation, denied access, destruction receipts, and principal-bound export-key delivery with deterministic identity, idempotent direct release, exact outcome lookup, exclusive-expiry/current-authority rejection before release, immutable Delivered outcome after release, and lost-ack recovery; tests cross expiry and actor revocation immediately before/after release, lookup outage, duplicate retry, cross-tenant substitution, changed purpose/audience/version, and stale/disconnected/restored migration writers while proving secret values do not enter events, projections, responses, logs, traces, or evidence. The live test also proves the non-public replay registrar credential can conditionally append only the exact replay stream/event and is unavailable to public, Workflow, and target-handler paths. Command: `TBD`.

fields.RequiredArtifact: Platform-owned host composition for the Agents DomainService and UI with EventStore, Conversations, Parties, Tenants, Provider and safety adapters, Dapr Workflow, secrets, health, identity, telemetry, and a replicated durable content-free `security-audit-spool`. The spool accepts a deterministic `SecurityObservationId` before a classified Agents denial returns, retains pending records across EventStore/replay outages, exposes exact-id outcome lookup/acknowledgement, and grants its drain worker an ACL restricted to the computed `SecurityEventLog(RoutingTenantId, UtcDay)` stream and event; if the spool itself is unavailable, ingress constructs no Agents command and platform health blocks tenant-access/audit readiness. The host additionally binds the production `EXT-PROTECTION-1` engine and exposes the FR-34 attestation port used at startup and every readiness evaluation. The port lets Agents seal a canary, prove persisted bytes contain no plaintext, unseal it, destroy its DEK, replay `Erased`, and obtain engine identity/version for comparison with the committed protection target; the host fails closed against both the no-op default and a self-reporting wrapper around it. For Story 6.1 it also composes the target-limited directory-migration Workflow and EventStore namespace ports. Installing a tenant migration epoch revokes the legacy direct-write credential/epoch, and every later interaction/failure create or content append requires the current epoch plus an exact directory permit or committed-effect capability. Every `ConversationAgentState` permit, creation/workflow-start/User-action-intent outbox, lease acquire/commit, and interaction-owned rate/open/Budget/capacity phase-authorization append is likewise conditional on the current directory capability at EventStore. Repair first atomically installs a directory-repair fence that revokes all those new-directory/effect-authorization operations and returns an authenticated checkpoint; only the post-fence finite permit/outbox/lease/phase-authorization cohort may enter the old-epoch bridge, whose exact pending/committed/authorized work drains before successor activation revokes the old epoch, repair fence, and bridge. For Story 8.3 the same port evaluates canonical `GovernanceScopeV1` and its predicate digest from authoritative tenant stream identity, immutable first-event/directory-permit `SourceConversationId`, and permit/action/lease/phase-authorization owner facts—never caller classification. Before either deletion origin builds a candidate, it conditionally installs a persistent ordinal scope admission fence that rejects later matching permit, User-action-intent, lease-acquire/commit, and rate/open/Budget/capacity phase-authorization appends; after the finite same-ordinal owner cycles become Effective it conditionally installs and verifies the separate content write fence that rejects later matching interaction/failure creates or content appends. The admission violation ledger is one append-only request ledger partitioned by fence ordinal: prior violations remain visible, while only the current installed ordinal can attest `ZeroAcceptedViolationsSinceInstall`. A pre-cut violation uses an explicit no-global-cut/candidate/token receipt; a later violation invalidates only exact present artifacts. Both assign one successor ordinal and require separately keyed owner cycles carrying all prior obligations. The content guard is stable by request/predicate and continuously installed: after one or more recuts, a successor-binding authorize/effect/result operation starts from the latest installed binding and appends the new ordinal/global-cut/token only after proving a complete gap-free ordered chain of intervening invalidated/tokenless ordinal receipts and the current zero proof; an overtaken authorization returns terminal obsolete without a guard append. The port also owns the tenant `GovernanceScopeGuard`: every authorized legal-hold request conditionally registers its canonical scope there before fence preparation and remains until an exact fully acknowledged release removes it. Hold registration and `CommitDeletionDestructionStartBarrierEffect` serialize on that owner. The `ProtectionFence` barrier authorization persists the exact observed `GovernanceScopeGuard` revision/compare token. Conditional append at that revision makes the seal operation serialize with admission writes and hold registration/release; an intervening mutation returns authenticated stale and must be mirrored before revision-bound reauthorization. The seal operation verifies both ledgers/current content binding/migration receipts, rejects any overlapping contender that won after authorization unless it consumes the exact effective deletion-allowed hold disposition, commits immutable `DestructionSealed`, and returns one deterministic non-expiring, revocable, single-use `DestroyDekManifest` capability bound to the sorted accepted key-target manifest; it has no `ExpiresAt` or renewal branch, and its capability-key version remains verifiable through outage, migration, restore, and the full retention of the batch identity and terminal outcome, including exact retry/lookup after consumption or revocation. No direct clean read, stale no-hold authorization, or unrelated append is authority. Each fence/guard/barrier exposes authenticated installation, exact-outcome lookup, verification/high-water, and complete append-only evidence; every admission ordinal/violation gap chain, owner cycle, content binding, hold contender/release, barrier/containment compare authorization and stale result, destruction seal, and batch identity/capability-key/guard-issued state plus referenced protection-owner blocked, reserved, re-attested, consumed, or revoked outcome survives migration successors. The protection engine consumes each manifest batch atomically as all targets or none, returns an ordered per-target irreversible receipt vector, and exposes exact batch lookup; each first previously uncovered complete protection target from an authoritative post-seal content violation is ProtectionFence-serialized into one monotonic ordinal and immutable singleton target manifest, while later same-target resources receive coverage links only, then follows `AuthorizeDeletionContainmentBatch`, guard-revision-conditional `CommitDeletionContainmentBatchEffect`, exact lookup, and `RecordDeletionContainmentBatchIssued` or `RecordDeletionContainmentBatchIssuanceStale` before its distinct batch may be consumed; exact duplicates reuse the ordinal/result and concurrent distinct targets receive distinct ordinals. An accepted admission after sealing invokes `BlockDeletionBatchConsumption` to race `ReserveAndConsumeDeletionBatch` at the protection owner, records `DeletionIntegrityCompromised`, blocks new batches, and can never be treated as resource-only content containment or successful completion. Missing, malformed, unknown-version, cross-tenant, or unverifiable scope membership rejects a write and prevents a clean verification result. The artifact replaces module-owned AppHost, Aspire, and ServiceDefaults ownership.
fields.CompatibilityContractAndVerificationComm: Contract: clean-checkout composition through the platform host without module-owned hosting infrastructure, including the durable security-audit spool, production protection-engine binding, and complete FR-34 attestation. The target-limited migration contract enforces the current epoch on interaction, directory, and effect-authorization writes; provides atomic directory-repair-fence install/checkpoint/lookup; freezes only the post-boundary cohort including protected User-action intents and rate/open/Budget/capacity authorizations; restricts the bridge to manifest-listed pending, committed, or already-authorized work; preserves every deletion fence ordinal/violation gap chain, owner-cycle receipt, continuous content binding, guard compare authorization/stale result, destruction seal, and batch capability/state; and atomically revokes old epoch/repair fence/bridge at successor activation. The deletion contract implements canonical exact-interaction and source-deletion exact-Conversation predicates; ordinal admission-fence authorize/effect/result; explicit pre-cut and post-cut violation containment with one successor ordinal; immutable separately keyed owner cycles and current zero proof; one continuously installed predicate content guard whose successor binding uses the latest installed binding plus a gap-free invalidation chain and returns terminal obsolete when overtaken; tenant-scope-guard revision/compare-token hold registration/release serialized with the destruction seal and authenticated stale reauthorization; an exact effective armed-contention disposition only when required; guard-owned atomic start-barrier authorize/effect/result; deterministic non-expiring, revocable, all-or-none manifest-batch destruction with per-target vectors, exact lookup and revocation race; guard-owned singleton containment-batch authorize/effect/result with ordinal allocation and lost-issuance lookup; migration preservation; post-start integrity blocking; and content containment with distinct batches. Tests race every directory/phase-authorization append and target write around migration-repair, admission-fence, and destruction-barrier boundaries; cover violations before the first cut and after content-fence installation; prove one successor ordinal, carried obligations, immutable Effective, repeated recut gap chains/obsolete binding outcomes, continuous content binding, and current zero; race hold registration/release before/at/after guard-revision-bound barrier authorization/seal while Open precedence stalls both and stale compare results require reauthorization; prove the guard commit—not a prior read—is first irreversible authority; and prove an exact multi-key manifest batch is consumed once, all targets or none, with non-expiring restore, lost-result lookup, revocation, explicit singleton containment issuance/lookup, and prior violations preserved. Human-origin exact-Conversation tests remain blocked pending `OD-HUMAN-EXACT-CONVERSATION-SCOPE-1`; `ClassUtcRange` tests remain blocked pending `OD-GOVERNANCE-CLASS-RANGE-SCOPE-1`. Command: `TBD`.
